If Not, Winter: Fragments of Sappho is a 2002 acclaimed collection of translated poetry by the archaic Greek poet Sappho, rendered into English by the Canadian poet and classicist Anne Carson.
Book Overview

* 
* Core Content: Features all surviving extant fragments of [Sappho's](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHrOzAVE8kTKWNcWsjlbxTXOOy4LqeADuns-vhHLaEmzj5vEHW3FjduLUpD3echt360j13Yd261RfwXk1kivuj9m0DxQt-ju9itzJap-Jd8ZOPhHwuM4cs_3k0U0yRbTYOL8hCe) verse from the island of Lesbos, presented alongside the original Greek text on facing pages.
Goodreads +1
* Origin of Title: Derived from [Anne Carson's](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESagHrOzAVWDt8OLfnOYusMOJBFdokjlS-kIL0amvFEbOl91UzOlMySv3NW7ZRtR14CRgdYLFqlVEiWCsuM0zGrdif7rHN3TdBmDxFjwaBCfKEKSo39Hr0v_datg7ZwWH0FHYw0b8wIapRhiM) translation of Fragment 22, which includes the evocative line “If not, winter . . . no pain”.
* Translation Style: Uses square brackets and deliberate white space to represent physical gaps, lacunae, and missing text from ancient papyrus scraps, allowing readers to visualize the fragmentary nature of the historical manuscripts. Users on [Reddit r/Poetry](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESmwEB6zswFRVuBaVX5azrYonu_gTK2yCwZRpjL-4h5HiYNdyTjTXi69wWyC4PtTr66WDwmHWsWdIWVUnsIKD75ztsbYXOA6xXoah9Jdus2uYljEyn-3QM1kgQZt9GpCvRJehs_aUnFqJm06dj1NfPjG72_SzYfOBfEZMRXwGp8SoGqMhIyHVjWuAd3YNV2RODH30Zj4QW3JGF_MnwNA) widely agree that Carson's choice to preserve these structural gaps powerfully amplifies the emotional resonance of the surviving text.
